profile.reading:
This building, VA14, sits on Vantage's Ashburn I campus at 45200 Vantage Data Plaza, Sterling, VA 20166, per this registry's address matching; Vantage does not publish an individual facility page or press release for VA14 specifically. Vantage's current campus page describes Ashburn I as 52 acres with six data centers totaling 1.7 million square feet at full buildout and 206 megawatts of critical IT load, a building count matching the VA11 through VA16 numbering tracked in this registry (VA11 at 30MW, VA12 at 32MW, and VA13 at 44MW are individually confirmed via Vantage press releases elsewhere in this registry), though Vantage does not explicitly confirm on its own site that VA14 specifically is one of the six, and no individual sqft or MW figure for VA14 is published anywhere found this session.

Vantage is a private, Denver, Colorado-headquartered operator; DigitalBridge acquired the company in March 2017, and in January 2024 Vantage announced a $6.4 billion equity investment round led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake. Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility: in November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates raising a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 data center rate class effective January 1, 2027, per Inside Climate News.

Northern Virginia's Loudoun and Prince William counties together form the largest data center market in the world by capacity, and local zoning debate has intensified as residents, county supervisors, and Dominion Energy weigh the tradeoff between commercial tax revenue and rising transmission-line construction, land consumption, and residential electricity-rate pressure tied to data center growth. Dominion Energy's long-range integrated resource plans have repeatedly cited this region's data center demand as the single largest driver of the utility's near-term generation and transmission capital spending, a dynamic that has drawn scrutiny from the Virginia State Corporation Commission in periodic rate cases. As documented in this profile's address and campus fields, this building's assignment to the Vantage campus it is grouped under is inferred from building-count and geographic proximity matching against Vantage's own published campus materials rather than from a Vantage-confirmed individual building name, so it should be read as a reasonable but unconfirmed placement pending direct operator confirmation.

reading.body:
Vantage Data Centers operates Ashburn I campus in Sterling, Virginia, a six-building facility totaling 206 megawatts of critical IT load and 1.7 million square feet at full buildout. VA14 is inferred to be one of these six buildings based on building-count matching and proximity, but Vantage publishes no individual power or square footage figure for VA14 itself. The three other Ashburn I buildings with published figures (VA11, VA12, VA13) range from 30 to 44 megawatts each, suggesting VA14's capacity lies somewhere in that range, though this is not confirmed.

Ashburn I sits in Northern Virginia, the world's largest data center market by aggregate capacity. The campus is ranked 24th among all published-capacity facilities in Virginia by the operator's disclosed figures, which represent only 23 of 330 mapped data center locations statewide. Virginia's electricity supply and cost structure are reshaping rapidly: in January 2027, Dominion Energy introduced a new GS-5 data center rate class, and residential rates rose by roughly 10 percent, driven directly by the region's data center demand as the single largest driver of the utility's transmission and generation spending.

No certification, power purchase agreement, or grid interconnection status is published for this facility. The binding constraint on Ashburn I's ability to scale remains Dominion Energy's transmission and generation capacity, which is now the explicit focus of Virginia's utility planning and rate regulation. Without published capacity figures for VA14 specifically, this building's individual role in AI infrastructure cannot be quantified from available sources.
